account:
Today I have been keeping my appointments: morning office hours, and now the ten-o'clock grain inspection at the east-bank mill. Council letters are due for review at thirteen, tea with my neighbour at fifteen, office business at sixteen-thirty, and a newly added great-hall meeting at eighteen. The secretary confirmed that the evening meeting concerns the innkeeper's community hospitality matter, that I should come alone without preparation, and that the secretary will remind and escort me. I do not yet know the substance of that matter.

There has been unusual activity around bread arrangements. Last evening I heard the baker calling to the builder, asking how many loaves had reached the hall, where freight was, and saying grain funding still needed settling. This morning my neighbour said the baker, freight, and innkeeper had been coordinating a bread order, but did not know the outcome. Those reports suggest supplies or hospitality preparations, possibly connected with the hall meeting, but I have no confirmation of that connection or of any completed deliveries.

At the mill just before ten, two townsfolk said 'bridge or port change at bakery.' I do not understand what change they mean, whether it is an actual transport change, or how they learned of it. I have just asked one of them for clarification and for someone to show me the grain stocks. Several townsfolk and my neighbour are nearby. I also heard my neighbour speaking moments ago but could not make out the words.

The town's financial paperwork remains incomplete: the secretary has not identified the accounts custodian, and no new council correspondence had arrived when we last discussed it. Yesterday the treasury contained 128 emeralds. I cannot yet establish any outstanding grain payment or other obligation from records. For now, bread coordination, the reported crossing change, and the evening hospitality appointment are matters to investigate rather than evidence of a definite shared plan.
